_doc: Access paths proven to hold a Direct3D 8 interface (or null), for com_calls.py. path: a global, then the offsets dereferenced in turn ([[global]+off]...). Each entry's `checks` are recomputed against the binary on every run; an entry whose check fails is not used. `proof` is the argument in full, `dumps` what the verified dumps of the analysed build show.

device_via_1047BFA8.proof: 0x1047BFA8 is written in two places: 0x1006B2D2 stores the object just constructed at 0x1006B2B0 (vtable 0x1032C0D8), and 0x1006B466 stores EDI, zeroed at 0x1006B3B8 and kept across the calls between (EDI is callee-saved in the MSVC x86 calling convention). Right after constructing it, 0x1006B2B0 calls 0x10069DD0 on it (ECX = the object) with the CDx* from 0x1045666C pushed as the argument; 0x10069DD0 is referred to nowhere else. 0x10069DD0 stores that argument at +0xDC8 (0x10069DE1, the only write of +0xDC8 in the binary) and at 0x10069E65 copies [[+0xDC8]+0xC] -- the CDx's pDevice, declared IDirect3DDevice8* in the IDB's CDx -- into +0xEBC (the only write of +0xEBC in the binary).
device_via_1047BFA8.dumps: In all four verified dumps (town, town2, combat, zonetoinn): [[0x1047BFA8]+0xDC8] == [0x1045666C] and [[0x1047BFA8]+0xEBC] == CDx->pDevice.
device_via_1047BFA8.depends: The last link, that the CDx's +0xC holds the device, rests on the IDB's CDx declaration (pDevice: IDirect3DDevice8*), written in this project from the constructor 0x100161B0 storing the D3D holder's device there; that no other instruction overwrites +0xC of that object afterwards is not shown (192 instructions write some [reg+0xC]). The four dumps agree with it.
